messages:

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 18 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Reserved capacity commitment — pricing protection and fallback

Vanessa,

Thanks again for walking us through the Dedicated offering yesterday. We’re excited about moving forward but want to lock down a practical protection if GPU market prices spike. Two asks from procurement: 

1) A mechanism to request a short-term credit/discount if the GPU spot/index rises more than X% over our baseline during the commitment term.
2) The ability to temporarily swap a portion of our reserved pool for a cheaper SKU (or burst to shared) while maintaining overall throughput guarantees, without penalty if exercised a limited number of times per quarter.

We’re looking at a 12–18 month reserve term on roughly 60% of our peak projected usage; the SOW (attached) has initial numbers. Can Redwood outline an approval path and what documentation you’d need to make this work (finance/legal sign-off, how triggers are computed, any impact to latency SLAs)?

Appreciate a short response that we can route to our CFO and procurement.

Best,
Amy Li
Head of Platform, Luminate
+1 415-555-0134

Amy —

Thanks for the clear asks and the SOW. High level we can support both ideas but we’ll need to codify precise triggers and an approval ladder. Quick proposal: 

- Pricing trigger: a GPU market index (we can use a public index + internal supplier pricing) — if average index over a 30-day window rises > 15% vs baseline we offer a temporary credit applied to invoices for that quarter. Credit size and cap would be subject to finance approval.

- Capacity swap: allow up to 2 swaps per quarter for up to 20% of reserved units; swaps could be to a compatible lower-cost SKU or to burst capacity on Hosted with a documented performance fallback. Each swap must be scheduled 5 business days in advance and will be limited to avoid KV cache cold-start penalties.

Next steps from our side: I’ve looped in Karthik (finance) and Marissa (head of sales ops) to scope the discount size, approval thresholds, and contractual language. I’m also attaching a short workflow doc that outlines operational steps. Can you confirm the target commit tenor and whether your legal team needs a PoC clause for the trigger calculation?

Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

Vanessa / Marissa —

Thanks — I ran preliminary math and governance thoughts below. I’m writing from a finance controls lens, so this is intentionally conservative: 

- Baseline: use the committed SKU effective price at contract signature (we’ll capture this in the SOW).
- Trigger: 30-day rolling index > 15% (relative) will open a credit window. 
- Credit sizing options (examples for discussion):
  * Option A: Fixed cap credit = 10% of quarterly invoice for the quarter of the spike (easy to underwrite).
  * Option B: Indexed credit = 60% of incremental delta between supplier index and baseline for tokens consumed during the spike window (closer match to cost, complex to audit).

- Swap governance: Allow swap up to 20% of reserved units for up to 30 days; swaps require written request and limit to 2 per quarter. Swaps may change per-token throughput cost and could affect latency SLOs — we should document acceptable bounds (e.g., 95th p50 latency increase < 20ms).

- Approval path: for credits above 8% of quarterly bill, require RevOps + Finance VP sign-off. For structural contract changes (term extension, SKU redefinition), legal review and CRO approval required.

Action items: 
1) Vanessa — propose which Credit Option you want to present to Luminate (A vs B), and prepare draft contract language.
2) Marissa — need a quick risk note for CRO: expected MRR impact under a 3-sigma GPU spike scenario.
3) Vanessa/Karthik — confirm whether Luminate’s requested 12–18 month tenor; moving to 18 months materially changes underwriting (we can offer slightly better baseline discount if tenure increases).

HubSpot: I’ve added a note on the deal (LF-9821) and linked a spreadsheet with model runs.

– Karthik
Finance, Redwood Inference

Amy / team —

Appreciate the patience here. My take after reviewing Karthik’s scenarios: we can sign off on a customer-facing construct that balances operational flexibility with predictable economics. Proposed commercial offer to present to Luminate: 

1) Term: 18 months committed on 60% of projected peak (per SOW). In exchange Redwood will offer a 6% baseline term discount.
2) Pricing protection: If the agreed GPU index rises > 18% (30-day rolling) we will grant a temporary credit equal to 12% of the invoice for that quarter, capped at 25% of total quarterly bill across all credits. Credits > 8% require RevOps + Finance VP approval (we’ll route).
3) Capacity swap: Up to 2 swaps per quarter, max 20% reserved units per swap, swaps limited to compatible SKUs we certify; swaps must be scheduled 5 business days in advance and will incur a $X operational coordination fee (covers cache priming support).

Operational notes: we’ll include exact trigger calculation language and a short attachment with the swap workflow in the contract exhibit. I’ll have Legal draft redline language and Finance will prepare an approval matrix for any credits. Vanessa — please present this to Amy and flag if they prefer Option A (fixed cap credit) vs Option B (indexed credit). If Luminate confirms 18 months we can improve the baseline discount to 7% — however that requires Exec Rev approval.

If Amy is comfortable with this framing I’ll brief RevOps + Legal and request sign-off.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
